reason: The cited evidence supports that selective oxidation of Al and Cr forms protective scales in HEAs (E3) and that a dense oxide layer can prevent further oxidation (E2), but none of the passages provide evidence that high configurational entropy retards diffusion of protective species or that this kinetic control is the governing mechanism. The core mechanistic premise linking entropy to diffusion kinetics is unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: Selective oxidation of minor high-affinity elements (Al, Cr, Si) forms protective oxide scales in HEAs
High configurational entropy in the HEA matrix retards diffusion of these protective species
Retarded diffusion enables formation of a continuous, dense, adherent oxide layer
This oxide layer acts as a barrier suppressing further oxidation and oxygen ingress
Increasing content of protective oxide formers improves oxide scale continuity and oxidation resistance
